data.title: bn-uwj7: resolve loop identity through a shared choke point
data.description:
risk:high — agent-identity resolution path (identity gates who can vote/merge).

WHAT: Extract responder + reviewer-loop --agent resolution into one pure fn config::resolve_loop_identity(agent_override, config). Behavior-preserving; both call sites reduce to agent_override.unwrap_or(config.default_agent()).

WHY: Regression bn-uwj7 (prior bd-3i5c/bd-2z38) — in rite hook context $AGENT/$RITE_AGENT are the message SENDER, not the loop's identity. A reviewer spawned for @project-security must not vote/merge as the sender. Both loops already resolved from the flag (never env); this removes the duplication so the two paths cannot drift and reintroduce sender-identity on only one.

FAILURE-MODE CHECKLIST (please verify):
1. Fail-closed on env: resolve_loop_identity never reads AGENT/RITE_AGENT (structurally — no env access). Confirm no path re-adds env fallback.
2. Behavior parity: responder's old 'agent.unwrap_or(default_agent)' (default_agent = config.map(default_agent).unwrap_or_default()) == new call with config.as_ref(). Reviewer-loop's old 'agent_override.or_else(project.default_agent).unwrap_or_else(default_agent())' == new call (config.default_agent already folds project.default_agent).
3. None-config edge: responder keeps empty-string default when config fails to load (unchanged).
4. Callers still set_var(AGENT/RITE_AGENT) to the resolved value AFTER resolution — confirm ordering unchanged so init-agent hook sees the loop identity.
5. Tests: real-AGENT env guard is serialized behind a Mutex and restores prior values before asserting.

data.body: INFO — Failure mode 1: What could fail in production? The realistic failure is a reviewer or responder loop adopting the WRONG identity and then voting/merging as it. This diff structurally removes the highest-risk variant (env-sender leakage) by never reading AGENT/RITE_AGENT. Residual failure surface: (a) responder resolves to EMPTY identity when config fails to load (agent=None, config=None -> "") — preserved from prior behavior, not introduced here; downstream seal/rite/bn would then act as "". (b) reviewer-loop cannot hit that branch: Config::load(...)? errors out before resolution, so the identity gate never silently becomes empty. No crash/corruption path is added.

INFO — Failure mode 2: How would we detect it quickly? A wrong-identity vote/merge is observable in seal review history (voter agent name) and rite messages (sender = resolved AGENT). An empty-identity responder shows AGENT="" in spawned-tool calls and in init-agent hook output. Detection is minutes-to-hours (manual/log inspection) — there is no active alert. Suggestion (non-blocking, out of scope for this behavior-preserving PR): a startup assertion that logs the resolved loop identity would make identity drift visible at spawn time rather than at vote time.

INFO — Failure mode 3: What is the fastest safe rollback? Trivial and data-migration-free. The change is a pure refactor extracting an identical expression into config::resolve_loop_identity; reverting the three hunks restores the two inline resolutions with zero state impact. Rollback = deployment/binary revert only (git revert of this commit), estimated seconds-to-minutes, no config change and no persisted-state cleanup required. No feature flag needed.

INFO — Failure mode 4: What dependency could invalidate this plan? The invariant depends on the rite hook contract that spawns loops with --agent set to the mentioned reviewer's own identity (not the sender). If a future hook-registration change (edict init/sync migration) dropped or mis-set --agent, the responder would silently fall back to the config default and the reviewer-loop to config.default_agent() — masking the misconfiguration rather than failing loudly. This function correctly refuses env, but it cannot detect a missing/incorrect flag. The spawn-side hook command (rite hooks add --mention ...) is the external dependency to keep in lockstep.

INFO — Failure mode 5: What assumption is least certain? The weakest link is the assumption that '--agent flag is always correctly supplied by the spawner.' The env-fallback removal is airtight, but identity correctness now rests entirely on the flag. Secondary less-certain assumption: that empty-string identity from a config-load failure is acceptable for the responder. It is preserved behavior, and the reviewer (vote/merge gate) is protected by Config::load(...)? erroring first — but an empty identity acting on rite/seal is a latent defense-in-depth gap worth a follow-up bone (reject empty resolved identity at spawn). Not blocking here since this PR is behavior-preserving.

data.reason: Security review passed. Behavior-preserving choke-point extraction; verified parity on both paths (responder empty-on-None-config and reviewer-loop project.default_agent fold both preserved). resolve_loop_identity structurally never reads AGENT/RITE_AGENT — the sender-identity regression cannot be reintroduced on only one path. set_var(resolve->set) ordering unchanged; env test guard serialized behind a mutex with restore-before-assert. No injection/secret/crypto/access-control concerns. Failure-mode checklist (5 INFO comments) posted; one non-blocking follow-up noted: reject empty resolved identity at spawn (defense-in-depth, pre-existing).
